comparison/Figure_1_CRAT_margins: Figure 1. CRAT minus the strongest non-CRAT mean in each metric and setting. Comparator selection is metric specific. Values are absolute score differences computed before rounding; no significance test is implied.
comparison/Figure_2_COMET_mean_SD: Figure 2. COMET performance of all adapted methods. Points are six-seed means and bars show ±1 reported SD. The horizontal scale differs across panels. Error bars do not represent uncertainty in a paired method difference.
comparison/Figure_3_quality_parameters: Figure 3. Observed BLEU versus trainable parameter count. The horizontal axis is logarithmic and vertical bars show ±1 reported SD. Zero-trainable-parameter base models are omitted. The dagger identifies the unequal training budget on Llama 2 EN-FR.
comparison/Figure_4_resource_ratios: Figure 4. CRAT-to-baseline ratios of reported means. Lower values favor CRAT for all four costs. Colors encode direction, not statistical significance. Training time in the dagger-marked setting reflects half as many CRAT updates and tokens.
ablation/Figure_1_quality_decreases: Figure 1. Absolute quality decreases relative to the displayed CRAT_full means. Each metric uses its own color scale; darker cells indicate a larger decrease. All 54 differences are recomputed from the primary means. The reference discrepancy in Appendix A affects every full-versus-ablation comparison. Color intensity does not indicate statistical significance.
ablation/Figure_2_resource_savings: Figure 2. Peak-memory and training-time reductions relative to the displayed CRAT_full resource values. Positive values indicate savings, and negative values indicate increased cost. Percentages use the primary measurements, with matched reported token counts within each pair. Timing uncertainty is not available.
ablation/Figure_3_causal_routing: Figure 3. Mean soft gates for CRAT_full and no_causal during training and evaluation. The dashed evaluation line marks the diagnostic threshold of 0.5. These are independent sigmoid gates recorded before evaluation top-k masking. No categorical normalization, gate variance, or executed-role frequency is implied.
sensitivity/Figure_1_matched_grid_sensit: Figure 1. Ranges of reported BLEU and chrF means on parameter grids shared by all three pairs. Shared values are 0.05/0.1/0.2 for KL, causal, and morphology coefficients; 0.001/0.005/0.01 for sparsity; 2/4/8 for temperature; 8/16/32 for rank; 32/64/96 for head budget; and 1/2/3/4 for top k. Each metric has its own color scale. Ranges describe sensitivity of means, not statistical uncertainty.
sensitivity/Figure_2_head_budget_tradeof: Figure 2. BLEU and chrF versus trainable parameter count under head-budget variation. Labels identify heads per direction. EN-FR bars show ±1 reported SD; no variability estimates are available for EN-FA or EN-ZH. Axis ranges vary by panel. Lines connect ordered tested budgets and do not imply that intermediate settings were evaluated.
sensitivity/Figure_3_topk_quality: Figure 3. Quality profiles across evaluation top-k settings. The dashed vertical line marks top k equal to 2. EN-FR bars show ±1 reported SD; absence of bars for EN-FA and EN-ZH reflects unavailable variability. Panel scales differ, and error bars are not paired confidence intervals for differences.
sensitivity/Figure_4_sparsity_and_gates: Figure 4. Evaluation mean soft gates across sparsity coefficients. The horizontal axis is logarithmic; EN-FR lacks the 0.2 setting. The dashed line marks the diagnostic threshold of 0.5. These gates precede top-k masking and are not categorical role probabilities.
integrated/Figure_1_baseline_margins: Figure 1. CRAT minus the strongest non-CRAT mean in each model-pair-metric comparison. Parentheses identify the metric-specific comparator. Positive differences favor CRAT. Each metric uses its own color scale, and no significance test is implied. Llama 2 EN-FR uses the unequal training budget noted in Table 2. Complete scores: Supplementary Analysis A, Tables 2 and 3.
integrated/Figure_2_ablation_resource_ch: Figure 2. Reductions in peak memory and training time relative to the displayed full-model resource row. Positive values indicate savings; negative values indicate increased cost. Reported training workloads match within each pair. Each panel has its own color scale. Timing variability is unavailable, and static roles represent a compound configuration change. Complete resources: Supplementary Analysis B, Table 2.
integrated/Figure_3_topk_quality: Figure 3. Translation quality across evaluation top-*k* settings. The dashed line marks *k* = 2. EN-FR error bars show ±1 reported SD; equivalent estimates are unavailable for EN-FA and EN-ZH. Panel scales differ. Error bars do not provide paired confidence intervals for the differences between settings. Complete measurements: Supplementary Analysis C, Table 4.
integrated/Figure_4_CRAT_without_KL: Figure 4. Resource savings and contextual quality comparisons for CRAT without KL. (a) Peak-memory and measured training-time reductions relative to full CRAT within each ablation workload. (b-d) CRAT without KL minus the Mistral Targeted SFT or LoRA mean; positive values favor CRAT without KL. Rows identify language pairs across all panels. Metric scales differ; COMET axis values are scaled by 1,000. Quality comparisons are descriptive: auxiliary backbone and seed provenance is unresolved, and the ablation uses 2.5 times the main-comparison updates. No paired uncertainty or significance is established (Supplementary Analyses A and B).
